clinician.trajectory_summary: A 58-year-old patient presented with a 3-month history of rapid, exponential growth of a round, hard, and not very mobile mass in the posterior femoral region, causing discomfort and embarrassment. Initial ultrasound revealed an extremely inhomogeneous formation with disorganized hypo-an-echogenic areas. MRI showed a lobulated lesion with an inhomogeneous signal (isointense in T1, hyperintense in T2, STIR, and PD) and focal central necrotic or cystic portions, without the typical 'fascia tail sign'. An excisional biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of high-grade myxofibrosarcoma (Grade 3 FNCLCC). Subsequently, the patient underwent a cycle of neoadjuvant radiotherapy and chemotherapy to increase local control rates and shrink the mass before planned definitive excisional surgery.
